Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $S^4=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have its unit round metric $g_X$. Denote by $p_\infty$ the point omitted by the north stereographic chart and by $p_0$ the point with north-chart coordinates $x=0$. Orient $S^4$ so that north-chart coordinates $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4)$ satisfy $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. Set $r^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2$. The metric in the north chart is $4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2$. Let $U_N=S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\}$ carry coordinate $x$, and $U_S=S^4\setminus\{p_0\}$ carry coordinate $y=x/r^2$; the metric in the south chart is $4(1+|y|^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dy^\mu)^2$.

Define $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$. Write $\epsilon_{123}=1$ and let

$$ \sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a. $$

The $T_a$ are traceless anti-Hermitian generators. Set $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$. Define antisymmetric symbols by $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $\bar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $\bar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for spatial indices $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, where $\delta_{ai}$ is the Kronecker delta; extend them antisymmetrically in the last two indices. For a scale parameter $\rho>0$, define $u(x)=(x^4I-i x^j\sigma_j)/r\in SU(2)$ on $U_N\cap U_S$. Form the quotient of the two trivial right $SU(2)$-bundles by identifying $(x,h)_S\sim(x,u(x)^{-1}h)_N$ for each $x\in U_N\cap U_S$ and $h\in SU(2)$, so its local sections satisfy $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. Take the set of admitted bundle sectors to be the singleton containing the isomorphism class of this glued bundle, and take the representation family to be the singleton defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$. Define the local connection potentials by

$$ A_N=\frac{2\eta_{a\mu\nu}x^\nu}{r^2+\rho^2}T_a\,dx^\mu,\qquad A_S=-\frac{2\rho^2\bar\eta_{a\mu\nu}y^\nu}{1+\rho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu. $$

On the overlap these obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_u A_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, so they define a smooth principal connection on the glued bundle. Let $F$ be its global curvature, with chart representatives $F_N$ and $F_S$. In the north chart its curvature, written $F_N=\tfrac12F^N_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu$, has components

$$ F^N_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{4\rho^2}{(r^2+\rho^2)^2}\eta_{a\mu\nu}T_a. $$

Let $*_{g_X}$ be the Hodge star characterized on two-forms by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_X$, acting componentwise on the Lie-algebra coefficients. This curvature is self-dual, meaning $F_N=*_{g_X}F_N$. With $B$ as fixed above, define the charge by $q_B=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge F)$ and, for any real $g>0$, define the action by $S_B(g)=g^{-2}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge *_{g_X}F)$. Then $q_B=1$, $S_B(g)=8\pi^2/g^2<\infty$, and the action saturates the self-dual bound. This is one explicit Belavin–Polyakov–Schwartz–Tyupkin (BPST) charge-one connection; no uniqueness or moduli classification is asserted.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=v^*w$ and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, of real dimension at least two. Its metric defines the $L^2$ pairing on forms by the Riemannian density; orientation is unnecessary. Let $d^*$ denote the formal adjoint of $d$, and $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ on total real forms, or on their complexification. With domain $H^2$ the operator is nonnegative and selfadjoint. Its degreewise smooth kernels $\mathcal H^k$ are finite dimensional, and there is an orthogonal smooth decomposition
$$\Omega^k(M)=\mathcal H^k\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d\Omega^{k-1}(M)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d^*\Omega^{k+1}(M).$$
The map $h\mapsto[h]$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^k\to H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$, over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ as appropriate.

More generally let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $m\ge1$ with a smooth Hermitian metric. Let $E$ be a holomorphic bundle of finite rank with a smooth Hermitian metric. The holomorphic bundle structure supplies frames with holomorphic invertible transition matrices; the Hermitian metric is separate smooth positive-definite pairing data. On $E$-valued $(p,q)$ forms, define $\bar\partial_E$ by the coefficientwise Dolbeault operator in holomorphic bundle charts and let $\bar\partial_E^*$ be its formal adjoint. For each fixed $p$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ on the sum over $q$ is nonnegative and selfadjoint on $H^2$; its smooth harmonic spaces $\mathcal H_E^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and
$$\Omega^{p,q}(X,E)=\mathcal H_E^{p,q}\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E\Omega^{p,q-1}(X,E)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E^*\Omega^{p,q+1}(X,E).$$
In particular harmonic forms represent the smooth Dolbeault quotient
$$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(X,E):=\ker\bar\partial_E/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_E$$
uniquely. Terms outside the degree range are zero. This asserts smooth Dolbeault cohomology; an identification with sheaf cohomology requires a separate Dolbeault-resolution comparison theorem.

For either complex write $D=d$ or $D=\bar\partial_E$, $P=DD^*+D^*D$, and let $\Pi,G$ be the preceding Green projection and inverse. They preserve degree, $G$ preserves smooth forms, and on smooth forms
$$DG=GD,\qquad D^*G=GD^*,\qquad D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0.$$
Every closed smooth $u$ satisfies $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$.
Assume countable choice. For $n\ge1$, $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(S^n)$ is $\mathbb R$ in degrees $0,n$ and zero otherwise. For $S^0$ it is $\mathbb R^2$ in degree zero and zero otherwise.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth-coefficient second-order differential operator on $E$, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)I_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors. Thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$; the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be an oriented smooth $n$-manifold with boundary, $n\geq1$, and let $\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)$. With $j:\partial M\hookrightarrow M$ and the outward-normal-first orientation,
$$\int_M d\eta=\int_{\partial M}j^*\eta.$$
An empty boundary contributes zero; in dimension one its integral is a finite signed sum of point values.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For an oriented orthonormal coframe let $\Omega_1=e^{14}+e^{23}$, $\Omega_2=e^{24}+e^{31}$, $\Omega_3=e^{34}+e^{12}$

Assume full AC. Give the unit sphere $S^4\subset\mathbb R^5$ its boundary orientation, round metric and standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean ball. Let $S=S^+\oplus S^-$ be its complex spinor bundle, with skew-Hermitian Clifford action $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2\langle v,w\rangle$ and positive chirality the $+1$ eigenspace of $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. A spin lift here is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ bundle double-covering the oriented orthonormal frame bundle; explicitly $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)\times Sp(1)$ covers $SO(4)$ by $(a,b):q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$ on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group, identified with $SU(2)$. The connection on spinors is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. Set $E=S^+$ with its rank-two Hermitian $SU(2)$ connection $A_+$.

The twisted chiral Dirac operator $D^+_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(S^4;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(S^4;S^-\otimes E)$ is Fredholm, with complex kernel dimension $1$, cokernel dimension $0$ and index $1$. In the anti-Hermitian Chern convention,

$$
\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_+}\wedge F_{A_+})=-1.
$$

Its positive trace-form instanton charge $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)$ is $1$; its connection is the scale-one self-dual BPST connection. More precisely there are parallel unitary identifications $F:\Lambda^0_{\mathbb C}\oplus\Lambda^2_{+,\mathbb C}\to S^+\otimes S^+$ and $G:\Lambda^1_{\mathbb C}\to S^-\otimes S^+$ under which

$$
G^{-1}D^+_{A_+}F(f,\omega)=df+\sqrt2\,d^*\omega.
$$

Here $\Lambda^2_+$ is the $+1$ Hodge-star subbundle, $d^*$ is the Riemannian formal adjoint, and all Sobolev spaces and adjoints use the specified bundle metrics. In the complete twisted spinor bundle the full Dirac operator is selfadjoint with domain $H^1$ and its square has domain $H^2$. This is a direct operator calculation for this explicit bundle, not an application of a general index formula.

derivations.claim: For any given spin four-manifold the local quaternionic model glues by its specified Spin(4) lift
Chirality anticommutes with $D_4$ and is parallel, so $D_5^2=D_4^2-\partial_t^2$
The constant central automorphism acts by $-1$ on both chiral spinor kernels and cokernels, and fixes the background connection
For any finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with anti-linear involution $J$, every $v$ has the unique decomposition $v=(v+Jv)/2+i(v-Jv)/(2i)$ with both displayed real components fixed by $J$
For antiperiodic boundary conditions the energy argument in step 1.2 would again force a zero mode to be constant in $t$, but a constant antiperiodic spinor is zero
The kernel parity, central inverse-determinant action and spin-clutch distinctions follow from the explicit Clifford construction, energy identity and finite exterior powers

boundaries.reason: The Statement fixes a nonempty round-sphere product and its actual rank-two twist.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.2 proves that the antiperiodic product kernel is zero.
Steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove one complex product zero mode and one real zero mode.
The Statement gives the N-fold determinant sign; for even N its value is1 by step 1.3.
Step 2.2 distinguishes the periodic, antiperiodic and center-gauge clutch signs rather than conflating them.
The Statement explicitly retains full AC through the source operator realization; the remaining real-form decomposition is explicit in step 2.1.
